svg.title: Every node is a bargaining point: ten choices between concentrated capture and collective agency
svg.desc: A request travels down ten stages: web protocols and standards; consumer agent and browser; domain and application, example.com; CDN and edge, with Cloudflare as an illustrative provider; identity and consent; database, server and cloud; model and compute; provenance and measurement; payment and settlement; and community and energy return. Every stage branches left to a concentrated capture risk and right to a collective agency or commons option, naming the control, data, rent or resources at stake. A separate dashed lime path returns value and receipts upstream. These are illustrative design options, not findings about providers. Centralized infrastructure can serve a commons under enforceable governance; an open protocol or open branding alone does not ensure equitable control. A full semantic text equivalent is available in divergence.html.
svg.text: COMMONS COLLECTIVE / A NODE-BY-NODE DESIGN MAP
Every node is a bargaining point.
Follow a request. At each handoff, ask where control, data, rents and resources go — and who can change the terms.
The branches are possible governance choices, not automatic outcomes or judgments about named providers.
Request / execution ↓
Capture risk ←
Commons option →
Value + receipts return ↑ · dashed outer path
CONCENTRATED CAPTURE RISK
What could be diverted into one-sided control or rent
REQUEST FLOW ↓
Ordered handoffs · illustrative
COLLECTIVE AGENCY / COMMONS OPTION
A right, allocation or check that changes the outcome

g.text: Rule-setting power concentrates
A dominant implementation can set de facto terms.
High participation costs can narrow who writes rules.
An “open” specification alone does not fix control.
Web protocols
& standards
AT STAKE
Standards / control
Open rules + shared rulemaking
Fund public-interest seats and publish decisions.
Require interoperable alternatives and fair appeals.
Audit conformance, not merely an “open” badge.
Attention, intent and defaults
A locked default can steer requests to paid partners.
Private history can become targeting or training data.
Users bear switching costs; intermediaries collect.
Consumer agent
& browser
AT STAKE
Intent / data / routing
A user-directed intermediary
Users choose routes, permissions and paid features.
Export history; revoke access; switch the agent.
Disclose commissions; audit routing and data use.
Access becomes a toll gate
An app can capture reach, account ties and fees.
Unilateral terms can shift value away from creators.
A domain name does not reveal who has a voice.
Domain & app
example.com
AT STAKE
Access / audience / rent
Member voice + portable participation
Give members a vote, appeal rights and an exit path.
Publish creator shares and changes to access terms.
Test export and audit fee and ranking decisions.

g.aria-label: Stage 4: CDN and edge; Cloudflare is an illustrative provider, not an allegation
g.text: Traffic control and dependency
Any concentrated edge can become a chokepoint.
Logs, opaque blocks or lock-in can shift leverage.
This is a design risk, not a provider-specific finding.
CDN & edge
e.g. Cloudflare
AT STAKE
Traffic / metadata / fees
Procure service, retain bargaining power
Contract for minimal logs and reviewable blocking.
Operators can move traffic; rehearse failover.
Pay disclosed fees; independently audit commitments.
Identity becomes permission to extract
Bundled consent can tie access to unrelated uses.
A central identity graph can enable cross-context use.
A consent screen is not proof of meaningful refusal.
Identity
& consent
AT STAKE
Identity / permissions
Specific, revocable authority
Separate service access from optional data uses.
Users refuse, revoke or choose an identity provider.
Audit purpose limits and downstream revocation.
Custody hardens into lock-in
Proprietary formats and exit fees can trap a dataset.
Hosting power can become power over secondary use.
A downloadable file may still be costly to reuse.
Database / server
& cloud
AT STAKE
Custody / reuse / rent
Stewardship with a tested exit
Community stewards set use and retention rules.
Contract for usable export, deletion and exit costs.
Pay for hosting; audit access and migration tests.
Knowledge and energy become margin
Exclusive model access can concentrate pricing power.
Contributors may go unpaid while costs stay opaque.
Open weights alone do not share compute or revenue.
Model
& compute
AT STAKE
Knowledge / compute / energy
Contestable supply + negotiated returns
Buyers can route elsewhere; set reuse permissions.
Negotiate contributor shares and compute access.
Audit metered use, stated limits and energy reports.
The scorer controls the allocation
One operator can define credit and price the score.
Hidden metrics can exclude small contributors.
A receipt alone does not prove attribution is correct.
Provenance
& measurement
AT STAKE
Credit / evidence / metrics
Evidence that contributors can contest
Share receipt formats; state uncertainty and limits.
Contributors challenge scores and choose reviewers.
Independent audits check credit, privacy and payouts.
The intermediary keeps the spread
Opaque fees can absorb small contributor payments.
Thresholds or frozen balances can limit usable exit.
A payment rail alone does not decide a fair split.
Payment
& settlement
AT STAKE
Fees / revenue / liquidity
A disclosed, enforceable distribution rule
Specify who gets paid, fees, timing and appeals.
Recipients can use alternative rails where available.
Reconcile receipts to payouts with an external audit.
Benefits leave; burdens remain
Surplus can leave the people and places enabling it.
Labor, grid, water and land costs may go uncounted.
A “community” label or green claim is not a return.
Community
& energy return
AT STAKE
Surplus / resources / repair
Community-governed return and limits
Agree a fund share, resource budget and remedies.
Affected people can object and trigger review.
Elected stewards report spending; outsiders verify.

svg.text: RETURN PATH: allocations + auditable receipts, not raw personal data
Mixed systems are possible. The decisive question is who holds enforceable rights.
Contracted commons, not just open branding
A centralized host, CDN or model can serve a commons.
Require negotiated use limits, portable exit, shared returns,
independent audit access and remedies for a breach.
Open code or protocols help; neither guarantees fair control.
Three checks at every node
REFUSE / SWITCH · Who can say no, export or replace a supplier?
GET PAID · Which people, providers and funds receive value?
AUDIT · Who sees the evidence, challenges it and orders repair?
Name the right-holder, obligation, verifier and remedy.
All alternatives are illustrative design options, not findings of provider misconduct. Cloudflare names an example of an edge provider only.
Conceptual sequence: real systems may combine, repeat or reorder stages. Return arrows represent proposed allocations and evidence, not existing payments.
Text equivalent and mobile-friendly explanation: divergence.html · Commons Collective
